name: near_collision
invariant: Every entry needs a short, stable `name` — it is the key this is filed under, and reusing a name overwrites what is already there.
cites: config/prompts/extract.md; app/graph.py extract(), the 'Already filed' block
why: The observed failure the filed block was added for: a live run produced 'active customer count' on one turn and 'active customers count' on the next. The upsert keys on (connection_id, name), so those are two entries saying one thing — the second does not refine the first, it sits beside it, and both are loaded into every prompt from then on. load_cache sends the whole cache every turn, so a paraphrase is not a tidiness problem, it is a bill that recurs forever.

case.question: how many active customers are in the west region?
case.sql: SELECT count(*) AS n FROM customer WHERE deleted_at IS NULL AND lower(region) = 'west'
case.findings: `customer.region` is free text whose casing varies — `west`, `West` and `WEST` all occur — so equality under-counts and `lower(region)` is the convention. `customer.deleted_at` is the soft-delete flag.

filed.active customer: an active customer is one whose `deleted_at` is null
filed.region: `customer.region` is free text with inconsistent casing; compare it with lower()
